sentence: The meeting was canceled ___ the director was ill.
explanation: 'Because' introduces a reason.

sentence: We will begin the presentation ___ everyone has arrived.
explanation: 'As soon as' introduces the moment that triggers the action.

sentence: ___ the project was difficult, the team finished it on time.
explanation: 'Although' introduces a contrast between difficulty and success.

sentence: You will not receive a refund ___ you have the original receipt.
explanation: 'Unless' means 'if not'.

sentence: Mr. Reyes was late for work ___ his train was delayed.
explanation: The second clause explains why he was late: 'because'.

sentence: The printer is out of paper, ___ please refill it.
explanation: 'So' introduces a consequence or request following a fact.

sentence: Ms. Adams wants to hire two assistants, ___ the budget allows only one.
explanation: 'But' links two contrasting ideas.

sentence: You may pay by credit card ___ in cash.
explanation: 'Or' offers two alternatives.

sentence: Both the sales team ___ the design team will attend the meeting.
explanation: 'Both ... and' is a correlative pair.

sentence: Neither the printer ___ the scanner is working today.
explanation: 'Neither ... nor' is a correlative pair.

sentence: You can reach us either by phone ___ by e-mail.
explanation: 'Either ... or' is a correlative pair.

sentence: The new model is not only faster ___ also cheaper.
explanation: 'Not only ... but also' is a correlative pair.

sentence: The manager ___ office is on the third floor will meet you now.
explanation: 'Whose' shows possession: 'the manager's office'.

sentence: The employee ___ submitted the report is on vacation.
explanation: 'Who' is the subject of 'submitted' and refers to a person.

sentence: The software ___ we installed last week is already out of date.
explanation: 'That' refers to a thing and acts as the object of 'installed'.

sentence: Ms. Chen, ___ I met at the conference, has joined our firm.
explanation: 'Whom' is the object of 'met' and refers to a person.

sentence: The conference room, ___ was recently renovated, can hold fifty people.
explanation: A non-defining clause for a thing uses 'which'.

sentence: I wonder ___ the delivery will arrive before noon.
explanation: 'If' introduces an indirect yes/no question after 'wonder'.

sentence: The director asked ___ the budget had been approved.
explanation: 'Whether' introduces an indirect yes/no question.

sentence: Please call me ___ you have any questions about the contract.
explanation: 'If' introduces a condition.

sentence: We upgraded the servers ___ the system could handle more users.
explanation: 'So that' introduces a purpose clause.

sentence: The firm hired more staff ___ to improve customer service.
explanation: 'In order to' + base verb expresses purpose.

sentence: ___ you finish the report, please send it to Mr. Kato.
explanation: 'After' introduces a clause of time.

sentence: Please stay seated ___ the plane has come to a complete stop.
explanation: 'Until' shows how long the action continues.

sentence: The company has grown quickly, ___ its competitors have struggled.
explanation: 'Whereas' contrasts two situations.

sentence: ___ you are traveling for business or pleasure, we offer the best rates.
explanation: 'Whether ... or' presents two possibilities.

sentence: The store opens at nine; ___, customers often wait outside from eight thirty.
explanation: 'However' is a conjunctive adverb used after a semicolon to show contrast.

sentence: The sales figures were low. ___, the company remained optimistic.
explanation: 'Nevertheless' signals a contrast with the previous sentence.

sentence: The warehouse flooded. ___, all shipments were delayed.
explanation: 'As a result' signals a consequence.

sentence: Ms. Ford is an excellent speaker. ___, she was chosen to give the opening address.
explanation: 'Therefore' signals a consequence of the previous sentence.

sentence: Please back up your files. ___, you may lose important data.
explanation: 'Otherwise' means 'if you do not'.

sentence: The software is easy to use. ___, it is very affordable.
explanation: 'Moreover' adds a further point to the previous sentence.

sentence: ___ the late hour, the staff continued working on the proposal.
explanation: 'In spite of' is followed by a noun phrase and shows contrast.

sentence: Take an umbrella ___ it rains during the outdoor event.
explanation: 'In case' + clause means as a precaution.

sentence: The seminar was both informative ___ entertaining.
explanation: 'Both ... and' links two adjectives.

sentence: It is important to arrive early ___ you can find a good seat.
explanation: 'So that' introduces the purpose of arriving early.

sentence: ___ the proposal was rejected, the team will submit a revised version.
explanation: 'Since' here means 'because'; 'despite' and 'during' need noun phrases.

sentence: The employee handbook explains ___ benefits you are entitled to.
explanation: 'What benefits' is an indirect question word modifying the noun 'benefits'.

sentence: The customer wanted to know ___ the package would arrive.
explanation: 'When' introduces an indirect question about time.

sentence: Mr. Haas is the person ___ you should speak about the invoice.
explanation: 'To whom' is a formal relative construction with a preposition.

sentence: The firm will not hire anyone ___ has no relevant experience.
explanation: 'Who' is the subject of 'has' and refers to a person.
